concerns.text: FR-001 references '(See US-1)' but no user story identifier 'US-1' exists; user stories are labeled 'User Story 1', 'User Story 2', etc. This creates an unresolved cross‑reference.
FR-002 also cites '(See US-1)' which is undefined, breaking traceability between requirements and user stories.
FR-003 cites '(See US-1)' yet no such identifier exists; the reference is invalid.

FR-004 mandates ±3σ outlier removal, but later comments (and the Constitution) note that roughness descriptors are often skewed, making the Gaussian assumption inappropriate. This conflicts with the principle of numerical stability.

FR-007 defines conditional CV folds (5 if n≥100, else 3) for hyperparameter tuning, while FR-013 repeats the same rule. Redundant but not contradictory; however the duplication may cause maintenance inconsistency.

Assumption states 'Data will have no missing values in material pairings', yet FR-003 and FR-010 describe handling missing material properties and imputation. This is a direct contradiction between assumptions and functional requirements.

The term 'pairing_id' is defined as linking a Material Pairing to a Data Point, implying uniqueness per experiment. Later comments and the Constitution (VI) require stratified splits by material pair, but the plan stratifies by 'pairing_id', which would be unique per row, causing data leakage. Terminology and intended grouping are inconsistent.

Constitution Principle VI specifies stratified splits by material pair, while the Feature Specification’s methodology (User Story 2 and FR‑007/013) mentions stratification by 'pairing_id'. The mismatch creates a scope shift without clarification.
The parenthetical after 'NIST Materials Data Repository' is empty '()' – missing citation or URL, breaking the requirement for a verifiable external source.
FR-010 uses statistical power < 0.8 or n < 200 to switch tests, but the effect size, variance, and alpha used for the power calculation are not specified anywhere, making the requirement untestable.
